20   Resolution Number 232, by Senator Kennedy, 

21   remembering and honoring the lives of the 

22   13 victims of Buffalo's November winter storm of 

23   2014.

24                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   I'm going 

25   to ask for some silence in the house, please.


                                                                235

 1                Senator Kennedy.

 2                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Yes, thank you, 

 3   Mr. President.

 4                As we prepare for a winter storm 

 5   today of unprecedented measure that's going to 

 6   hit the Northeast, I rise to remember and honor 

 7   the 13 victims of Buffalo's November storm just 

 8   this past 2014.  We send our thoughts and prayers 

 9   to the families and friends as they mourn the 

10   loss of their loved ones.  

11                On the evening of Monday, 

12   November 17th, an epic winter storm began that 

13   would devastate Buffalo and all of Western 

14   New York.  Lasting four days, millions of dollars 

15   would be spent in cleanup and rescue operations, 

16   making this one of the costliest storms in 

17   regional history.  

18                But the financial cost pales in 

19   comparison to the human cost.  There are 

20   13 families with an empty seat at the table and a 

21   hole in their heart that will never be filled.  

22   Today we join the entire Western New York 

23   community as we regretfully mourn and remember 

24   the lives lost:  Stephen H. Thomas, Cynthia 

25   Woodrick, Michael N. Strachan, Lyle H. Hull, Sr., 


                                                                236

 1   Ruth R. Snyder, Valentine L. Mozdziak, John 

 2   "Jack" Boyce, James A. Thomas, Sr., Jan Barsam, 

 3   David M. Deneke, Donald J. Abate, Robert M. 

 4   Cedar, and Delancey Scott, who all passed away as 

 5   a result of this devastating storm.

 6                Mr. Scott's mother, Barnette Burton, 

 7   is here with us today on the Senate floor as we 

 8   honor the memory of her firstborn son.  Thank you 

 9   very much for joining us here today in your son's 

10   memory.

11                (Applause.)

12                SENATOR KENNEDY:   We as a chamber 

13   offer our most sincere regrets and most heartfelt 

14   condolences on your loss.

15                We mourn all of the lives lost as a 

16   city, as a region, and as a state.  While we 

17   cannot bring back their loved ones, families of 

18   the victims of the storm can take comfort in 

19   knowing that their legacy will live on.  

20                Even in the darkest points of the 

21   storm, there were still points of light.  During 

22   this storm our community banded together in a 

23   tremendous way.  We saw people not only helping 

24   friends and family but aiding neighbors and even 

25   strangers in their time of need.  


                                                                237

 1                On my street in South Buffalo, we 

 2   were snowed in for four days.  It was tough, but 

 3   it brought us all closer together.  Neighbors 

 4   checked in on seniors, making sure that they were 

 5   warm and fed; families got together for meals all 

 6   throughout our region; and we all helped shovel 

 7   and clear snow.  

 8                From neighbors helping each other to 

 9   dig out their homes, to residents taking in a 

10   stranded traveler, to firemen in South Buffalo 

11   helping to deliver a baby, we were reminded that 

12   the City of Buffalo is truly the City of 

13   Good Neighbors.  It was an extremely difficult 

14   time, but we came together as neighbors, as a 

15   state, as a community to help one another.

16                Tragically, there were those whose 

17   lives were lost in this unprecedented disaster.  

18   As we honor them today, their families can rest 

19   assured that their memory will live on in 

20   perpetuity.

21                Again, Mr. President, I thank you 

22   for the privilege.  And we honor those who were 

23   lost in the November storm.  May they rest in 

24   peace.  

25                Thank you, Mr. President.

20   to honor her son, Delancey Scott, who we lost in

24   passed away alone, and she wanted to be here 

25   today so that in a small way she would be with

20                SENATOR KLEIN:   Thank you, 

21   Mr. President.  

22                This legislation would prohibit 

23   placing Level 2 and 3 sexual predators in any 

24   temporary emergency housing or homeless shelter 

25   used to house families with children.  This is a 


                                                                245

 1   problem, unfortunately, that has existed for some 

 2   time, that family shelters that have children, in 

 3   the City of New York under the auspices of the 

 4   Division of Homeless Services, have sexual 

 5   predators among children.  

 6                You know, I certainly understand the 

 7   mandate and need to house the homeless, that 

 8   someone should be guaranteed that they have a 

 9   shelter upon demand.  But to have a policy in 

10   place which is so shortsighted, to have a policy 

11   in place which puts children in homeless 

12   facilities in jeopardy each and every day, makes 

13   absolutely no sense.  If indeed someone is found 

14   to be a dangerous sexual predator, put them in a 

15   men's-only shelter.  Put them in a shelter that 

16   doesn't have any children.  You know, give them 

17   the right to have shelter, but do not put a 

18   ticking time bomb, which is a sexual predator, 

19   endangering the lives of children in homeless 

20   shelter facilities.  

21                So I vote yes, Mr. President.
